terms.storyLine: A whole work, owned by you and handed to a Reader as one link.
terms.sceneLine: A linear run of Shots, and the only unit at which a Story branches.
terms.shotLine: One beat: an image, its text, or both. The smallest thing a Reader is shown.
terms.exitLine: A way on from one Scene to another, offered at the end of a Scene for the Reader to take.
terms.conditionLine: A test that decides whether a Shot plays or an Exit is offered, so the same Scene reads differently without ever branching.

step.heading: Next
step.dismiss: I can take it from here
step.nameScene: Every Story starts with a Scene. Write the first one here: it lands on the bench and opens for writing, with its name selected — so “The arrival” is the first thing you type.
step.writeShot: A Shot is an Image and its text, as much as the Reader is shown at once. Add one, and write the first thing they read.
step.drawExit: An Exit is the way on, and a Story branches between Scenes rather than inside one. Drag from the edge of this Scene onto the bare bench and let go: a second Scene is made where you dropped it, already joined and open to be named.
step.setFlag: State is what one Reading carries with it. Give this Scene a Flag — “courage = high” — and it is set on every Reader who enters.
step.openingScene: A Reading has to start somewhere, and nothing marks where this Story does. Write a Scene and mark it as the one to start on — any of them will do, and you can name another whenever you like.
step.putCondition: A Condition makes the same Scene play differently to different Readers, without branching. Write the second Scene, add a Shot, and have it played when that Flag holds something else — “low” will do. Nothing plays it yet, which is the point.
step.previewCondition: Nothing plays that Shot, and the Preview beside the Scene says why: it reads the Story on the engine a Reader runs, and shows what each Shot it skipped asked for beside what the State actually holds. Read that, then put the value right.
step.publish: That is a Story that works. Publish it, and anybody can read it at a link of its own — the one this page then shows, to hand to whoever you wrote it for.

refusals.badCondition: A Condition tests what one Flag holds, or how often one Scene has been entered, up to {max} times.
refusals.exitTextLong: An Exit cannot carry more than {max} characters.
refusals.exitTarget: An Exit arrives at a Scene.
refusals.sceneNameLong: A name cannot be longer than {max} characters.
refusals.scenePlacement: A Scene sits between 0 and {reach} pixels from the graph's corner.
refusals.tooManyFlags: A Scene cannot set more than {max} Flags.
refusals.badFlag: A Flag is a name and a value, and neither of them may be left empty.
refusals.tooManyFlagValues: A Flag cannot be drawn from more than {max} values.

refusals.storyTitleLong: A title cannot be longer than {max} characters.
refusals.storyLanguage: A Story is written in one language.
refusals.storySynopsisLong: A Synopsis cannot be longer than {max} characters.
refusals.shotTextLong: A Shot cannot hold more than {max} characters.
refusals.description: A Description says what an image shows, in at most {max} characters.
refusals.imageMissing: An image is a file to upload.
refusals.imageHeavy: An image cannot weigh more than {mb} MB.
refusals.imageType: A Shot carries a JPEG, a PNG or a WebP image, and nothing else.
refusals.authorName: A Name is what you appear under, so it cannot be empty.
refusals.authorNameLong: A Name cannot be longer than {max} characters.
refusals.nameBeforeListing: A Story is listed under its Author's Name, so write yours before listing it.
refusals.listPublished: A Story is published before it is listed, because an entry in the Catalogue leads to its public link.
refusals.openingScene: A Story needs an opening Scene before it can be published. Write a Scene on the graph and mark it as the one to start on.
refusals.signedOut: You are no longer signed in, so nothing was written.
refusals.commentText: A Comment carries what you have to say, so it cannot be empty.
refusals.commentTextLong: A Comment cannot be longer than {max} characters.
refusals.nameBeforeCommenting: A Comment is signed with its Author's Name, so write yours on the list of your own Stories before commenting.
refusals.listTitle: A List gathers Stories under a title, so it cannot be empty.
refusals.listTitleLong: A title cannot be longer than {max} characters.
